title: Automated by default; approval wherever authority or consequence is involved
prompt: How does the platform determine which development activities can be automated and which ones require human approval?
summary: PL automates analysis, drafting, generation, verification and packaging. It requires a typed human decision for anything that fixes intent (Blueprint, requirements), authorizes execution (Start build), accepts a result (Business Review) or reaches outside the workspace (external effects).

rows: Accepting a default, approving the Blueprint and Requirements
Start build; activation after Business Review
Fresh, exact authorization for each external effect
Token and model-call ceilings per turn and session
Rolling over to a successor chat

rows.label: How it is enforced
rows.value: A policy engine restricts each step to allowed action types; tools are authorized against fingerprinted step descriptors; approvals must be caused by an authenticated user event; external side effects need a task envelope, an effect grant and governance policy.

rows.label: Why it feels light
rows.value: Approvals are typed cards, not forms. A first application needs about eight clicks of authority in total.

plPrompts.label: Ask PL what it will not do alone
plPrompts.prompt: Which development activities do you automate and which ones require my approval? Distinguish proposals from authorized execution. Do not build anything.

title: Who plays which role during delivery
prompt: What roles do AI agents, developers, architects, testers, product owners, and business users play during application delivery?
summary: Business users and product owners own intent and acceptance; developers and architects own design review and evolution; testers own evidence review; PL's agents draft, generate and verify; operators run the platform. Roles are collaborative, not sequential.

rows: Owns the problem and the outcome
Describe, answer questions, accept defaults, approve Blueprint and Requirements, accept the release, use the app in EAL
Decide what is in the first version and what is deferred; approve changes and their impact
Confirm the landscape; review the Solution Design; decide integration approach
Review the Build Plan; request precise changes; use coding assistance; evolve the app
Read Business Review checks; reject with reasons; add acceptance signals to Requirements
Understanding, discovery, drafting, generation, verification, evaluation
Never approve, never build without Start build, never act outside the workspace
Control Center: start, stop, monitor; EAL activation and revocation

blocks.text: One person can play every role for a small application; the platform does not force a role questionnaire. It adapts to the task and to your stated preference for guided or direct interaction.

plPrompts.label: Ask PL about roles
plPrompts.prompt: What roles do AI agents, developers, architects, testers, product owners, and business users play during application delivery on this platform? Do not build anything.

title: Traceability, deterministic generation and evidence keep applications correct
prompt: How does the platform ensure that generated applications meet requirements and are technically correct?
summary: Requirements trace to acceptance criteria and tests; generation is deterministic from the approved Blueprint; every build runs typecheck, tests and a browser qualification with independently supplied expected values; hashes and receipts make the result reviewable.

blocks.caption: The traceability engine assembles this matrix; the Business Review shows it.

rows.label: Meets requirements
rows.value: A traceability matrix links requirements to criteria and tests; browser qualification drives the running app with a business oracle whose expected values come from outside the model.

rows.label: Technically correct
rows.value: Deterministic generators produce typed domain, API and UI code; typecheck, unit and contract tests, build and start must pass; ports, schema and identity are verified after deployment, not assumed.

rows.label: Secure by construction
rows.value: Generated APIs enforce per-action authorization and idempotency receipts; the app runs with its own database login; EAL authority is resolved live for every request.

rows.label: Reviewable
rows.value: Artifact manifests with SHA-256 per file, immutable release directories, provenance gate on commits, delivery journal with every receipt.

blocks.text: Correctness is proven for what was specified. If a rule is missing from Requirements, no test will catch it; that is why the guide keeps sending you back to Requirements for changes.

plPrompts.label: Ask PL how it verifies apps
plPrompts.prompt: How does the platform ensure that generated applications meet requirements and are technically correct? Name the checks that run at build and review time. Do not build anything.

title: Testing, validation, review, security and quality checks in detail
prompt: How are testing, validation, code review, security review, and quality checks handled?
summary: Automated: typecheck, generated contract tests, build, start, browser qualification, hash verification, generated-security refinements. Human: work-product reviews and Business Review. Platform-level: Eval Studio campaigns with sealed evidence and an independent register of gaps.

layers.title: Every build (automated)
items: Build and start on reserved ports

layers.title: Security (automated at generation)
items: Own database login, no platform secrets

rows: Build Plan and Solution Design review
Platform; generated-security eval scripts in the apps repository
Existing tests must pass before a new version
Eval Studio, with work items resolved and re-verified

blocks.text: There is no separate manual security sign-off gate today. Security controls are generated into the application and evaluated by scripts; a formal review gate is part of the customer-readiness work.

title: Readiness is a set of typed gates, each backed by evidence
prompt: How does the platform know when an application is ready to move from development to testing and then to production?
summary: Within Local Development: Blueprint approved, landscape confirmed, four heads approved on the active revision, build verified, Business Review accepted. Promotion to QA and Production is planned to work by immutable release manifests passing environment gates.

items.label: Ready to specify
items.detail: Enough discovery dimensions covered; no semantic defects; Blueprint approved

items.label: Ready to build
items.detail: Requirements, Delivery Plan, Solution Design, Build Plan approved on the active revision; budget available

items.label: Ready to review
items.detail: Typecheck, tests, build, start and browser qualification passed; release identity recorded

items.label: Ready to use
items.detail: Business Review accepted; release activated in EAL; roles in UME

items.label: Ready to promote (planned)
items.detail: Release manifest with evidence passes the QA, UAT and Production gates

rows.label: Never inferred from chat
rows.value: Readiness is computed from delivery-case state and receipts. A message saying it is ready changes nothing.

rows.label: Refusals are explicit
rows.value: Start build before the heads are eligible is refused with the missing item; a build without budget is refused with the shortfall.

rows.label: Gate artifacts
rows.value: Each gate writes a JSON and Markdown record with hashes so later reviews can verify what passed.

plPrompts.label: Ask PL whether this project is ready to build
plPrompts.prompt: Is the current application ready for Start build? List which work products are approved on the active revision and what is still missing. Do not build anything.

title: Errors are surfaced with their step and a proposed next action
prompt: How are errors, failed builds, failed tests, or deployment problems handled?
summary: Build steps report the failing step and output; a failed session accepts Start build again after the cause is fixed; deployment problems are auto-resolved where safe (ports) or refused with a code; activation can roll back; budget and model-call limits have explicit recoveries.

rows: Stops the build at Verify; shows the failing check
Fix the rule in Requirements (or accept PL's proposed correction); rebuild
Reserves another port and updates the release
Reports the step and the compiler output; session status becomes failed
Send Start build. again after the fix; a failed session accepts it
Refuses with a code such as PL_APPLICATION_MIGRATION_IMMUTABLE_CONFLICT
Use the recovery the message names; never edit files by hand
Conditional activation; rollback to the previous release
Answer defaults one card at a time; avoid apply everything
Roll over to the successor chat and continue

blocks.text: Every failure leaves receipts in the delivery journal, so a retry never repeats a committed effect: idempotency keys, durable effect records and fencing protect against duplicates.
